title: What If the Passenger Pigeon Had Never Gone Extinct?

scenes.text: What if the most common bird in America never vanished? It numbered in the billions.
Estimates run as high as 3 to 5 billion passenger pigeons in the 1800s.
One flock in Ontario in 1866 was reportedly 300 miles long and darkened the sky for 14 hours.
They were easy to catch and cheap to sell, and forests were being cleared at the same time.
By 1900 the wild birds were gone. In 1914, the last one, Martha, died at the Cincinnati Zoo.
Billions of birds to zero in about a century. Scientists now debate bringing the species back.

description:
What if the passenger pigeon had never gone extinct?
It was once the most abundant bird in America, with billions flying in flocks that blocked the sun.
